sources.reference: src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro (meta + og:description), src/components/PostCard.astro (card blurb), src/pages/index.xml.ts (RSS item)

Seth in chat 2026-10-27: the agent writes the missing descriptions ('that's your writing, get on it'); best-for-SEO is the goal; 2026-10-27 follow-up: descriptions must tease ('I'll show you how to be sure your function really...'), not spoil each post

prohibitedClaims: Any fact, result, or recommendation the page itself does not contain
Outcome promises stronger than the post makes (e.g. a guaranteed fix where the post reports what worked for the author)
Presenting a 2014-era post (SPDY, PageSpeed Insights scores, Ghost, Dreamhost email pricing) as current advice
Promising part 4 of the reverse-proxy series, which is unpublished
Videos or posts that do not exist on the site
constraints: One description per page, authored individually with that page's source open; no template or token swap
Roughly 110-160 characters so Google shows it untruncated; a single sentence or two short ones
Reads correctly in all four places it renders: search snippet, social preview, RSS item, and the post-card blurb on /posts/ and tag pages
Seth's register: plain, direct, first person allowed, no hype words, no marketing CTA
Do not edit migrated post bodies (R14); the change is frontmatter only, plus a description prop on the two list routes
Tease, do not spoil: name the problem and promise what the post shows, but never give away the answer, fix, number or list itself (Seth, 2026-10-27)

pageJob.reader: A developer, homelabber or tinkerer who sees a ByteMyCache page in Google results, a shared link, RSS, or a post card
pageJob.state: Scanning several options and deciding which one actually covers their problem or interest
pageJob.action: Decide quickly whether this page is the one to open, or skip it

sources.reference: Google Search Central, 'Control your snippets in search results' (meta description guidance: unique per page, accurate summary, specific facts over keyword lists); from prior knowledge, not re-fetched this session
Site render path: description doubles as card blurb and RSS item (render:surfaces)

readerDecisions: Is this page about my exact problem or topic?
Will it give me a fix, a how-to, or an opinion?
Is it current enough to trust?
proofPatterns: The concrete thing the page delivers (the fix, the steps, the tools named)
The specific stack or product names a searcher would type
notForegrounded: Generic CTAs such as 'read more' or 'click here'

questionSequence.question: What, specifically, is this page about?
What will I get from it: a fix, a walkthrough, a list, or an opinion?
Is there anything about its age or scope I should know before I click?

argumentMap.belief: The reader can tell at a glance which exact problem, tool or topic the page covers.
The reader knows what kind of payoff the page offers and wants it, without the description handing it over.
Where age or scope changes whether the page helps (2014 posts, a multi-part series), the reader learns it before clicking.

contract.maximalHonestPromise: Each description tells the reader exactly what problem the page tackles and what it will show them, with nothing the page does not deliver.
contract.signedThesis: A specific, honest one-line teaser in Seth's plain voice gets the right readers to click and lets the wrong ones skip.

deliberateOmissions.reason: Google ignores them and they read badly on cards and in RSS.
The card and the search result are already links; a CTA wastes the character budget.
Google and the cards show the date; age is mentioned only where it changes whether the advice holds.
Already on the page; it does not help a searcher decide.

lensReview.rationale: Names the subject in terms a searcher types.
Lets the reader judge whether the page answers their need.
Prevents a click that the reader would regret because of age or scope.
